direction: Keep the L2a static parallel-merge skeleton but make the savings score a global-scale-normalized generalized savings with capacity-fill and endpoint-demand-balance terms, and close the documented 'no post-merge inter-route relocate' gap by pairing it with relocate_2opt polishing to repair residual route fragmentation on tight-capacity / eccentric-depot instances.

operations.mechanism: Round 1 (L2a + intra_2opt) reached 16.0798 mean at ~2.1 ms/instance, leaving ~497 ms of unused budget. The verified KB entry method-cvrp-m2-l2a-generalized-savings fixes the safe scoring family (global depot-distance scale, lam 1.00-1.15, mu 0.08-0.15, beta 0.05-0.15, dimensionless fill reward, explicit pitfall against per-pair normalization) and states its only weak regime is 'no post_merge_inter_route_relocate' — exactly the untested combination it lists under unconfirmed items (L2a + relocate_2opt). Since dev_24's weakest regimes are tight capacity (vbs -21.7%), size 100 (-20.9%) and eccentric depot (-19.3%), where merge construction tends to leave under-filled end routes, adding inter-route relocate + 2opt polishing after the evolved merge is the highest-leverage, time-affordable change; the L2b attribution evidence (dynamic refresh = zero objective gain but 3.7x p95 cost) tells us to spend the budget on postprocess moves rather than on dynamic candidate refresh.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: H1: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24, score(i,j) = (d0i + d0j - lam*dij + mu*|d0i - d0j|)/mean(d0[1:]) + beta*clip((qi+qj)/Q,0,1) + gamma*(1 - |qi-qj|/(qi+qj)) with lam~1.05, mu~0.12, beta~0.10, gamma~0.05 (never per-pair normalization) will keep the merge layer near the 16.14 dev_24 level while the relocate_2opt postprocess removes residual inter-route fragmentation, so the combined solver beats the round-1 baseline mean objective 16.0798 (especially in the weakest regimes: tight capacity, eccentric depot, n=100) within 500 ms per instance.
